newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Artemis has no comment on state offer.
newsitem.headline: France's Artemis has no comment on state offer.

text.p: French holding company Artemis declined comment on Friday on a bid by a state agency to buy one quarter of the firm that controls a wide range of assets, including retail empire Pinault-Printemps-Redoute.

State-owned holding company EPFR made an 11th-hour offer to buy state-owned bank Credit Lyonnais's stake in the company to prevent Artemis' majority owner, Francois Pinault, buying it for a rock-bottom price.
A source close to the transaction said Artemis, which is unlisted, has 15 days to decide whether to seek to trump the state's bid with a counter-offer.
Under a deal signed last year, Pinault was given the right to buy the bank's 24.5 percent stake in Artemis for just 1.5 billion francs ($261 million) if no other buyer was found by May 31, 1997.

The agreement was struck with the Consortium de Realisation (CDR), a company established in 1995 under a state-backed rescue of Credit Lyonnais to take over and sell around 200 billion francs of the bank's assets, including the Artemis stake.
EPFR, which made the offer for Artemis, is the parent company of CDR.

The stake was valued on CDR's books at 3.7 billion francs. Press reports said it could be worth five billion francs but a source close to the CDR said such a figure ignored its debt and the fact the 24.5 percent stake was a minority holding "which diminishes its value".

Pinault, who holds 75.5 percent of Artemis, built up the holding company with the help of Credit Lyonnais during the bank's heady expansion before it nearly collapsed under the weight of its lending excesses.

Artemis was one of the few sound investments made by Credit Lyonnais under former chairman Jean-Yves Haberer who wanted to promote the bank's involvement in industry using the German model in which banks often take stakes in major clients.
The sale of the Artemis stake at a bargain price to Pinault would have meant French taxpayers would have suffered another loss as a result of Credit Lyonnais.
CDR's total losses on sales of Credit Lyonnais assets, bought at the peak of the market, and from carrying costs could hit 150 billion francs, published reports say.
The newspaper Liberation said treasury officials believe the CDR has been selling the assets too quickly and too cheaply but the CDR says the criticism is unfounded.
Artemis controls a wide range of assets including Pinault-Printemps-Redoute, renowned Bordeaux vineyard Chateau Latour, stakes in a raft of U.S. businesses and a portfolio of junk bonds.

The CDR gave investment bank Goldman Sachs the mandate to seek a buyer for its Artemis stake but the few offers received were not high enough and potential buyers were reported to be reluctant to be minority shareholders in an unlisted company.
-- Penny MacRae, Paris Newsroom +33 1 4221 5452 ($ = 5.747 French Francs)
